did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a musical heading, “For the choirmaster, with stringed instruments,” and its heading attributes it to David.
Did you know? The prayer opens with two verbs of listening—“Hear” and “Listen”—emphasizing the psalmist’s request that God attend to his cry and prayer.
Did you know? The psalmist describes himself as being “at the ends of the earth,” with his heart fainting—that is, in distress. In this state, he asks God to lead him to a rock higher than he is.
Did you know? God is described here with two images of protection and security: a “refuge” and a “strong tower” against the enemy.
Did you know? The psalmist asks to dwell in God’s tent “forever” and take refuge under the shelter of His wings—a picture of abiding continually under divine protection.
Did you know? The psalmist combines thanksgiving with a request: he notes that God has heard his vows and has given an inheritance to those who fear His name.
Did you know? Beginning with this verse, the prayer focuses on the king: the psalmist asks that his days and years be extended, “through all generations.”
Did you know? The psalmist asks that the king be enthroned forever before God, and that steadfast love and truth protect him.
Did you know? The psalm ends with a personal commitment: the psalmist will sing praise to God’s name forever and fulfill his vows day after day.
